title: Specify command and actuator limits
brief: Specify an instrument that separates available capacity, applied command, and actuator timing. Static capacity alone must not unlock a time-critical claim.
supplied: Can a commanded elevator response be delivered within the available travel and time, while keeping capacity distinct from applied moment?
M_applied=u*available; 0<=u<=1. Required normalized command=(Iy*target-other)/available. For this synthetic actuator case, timeNeeded=travelDeg/rateDegPerSec.
available=4002.48 N m; Iy=5000; target=0.12 rad/s²; other=-750 N m. Synthetic actuator demand travel=12 deg, rate=20 deg/s, deadline=0.4 s.
Available capacity, applied moment (N m), normalized command, slew time (s), and separate static/rate statuses.
The linear command map is a teaching approximation. Constant actuator slew rate ignores load dependence; no validated hinge-moment or pilot-force model is supplied.
A favorable static moment margin does not establish timely delivery or real elevator aerodynamics.
Half command applies 2001.24 N m; capacity remains 4002.48 N m. The 12° movement takes 0.6 s and misses the 0.4 s deadline.
1350/4002.48≈0.33729 command for the initial acceleration target. 12/20=0.6 s; 0.6>0.4.
Check u=0, 0.5, 1; reject u outside [0,1]. Show that static capacity passes while the synthetic rate deadline fails.
Sweep u and calculate applied moment and net initial acceleration. Independently compare actuator time with the declared deadline.
Retain the steady-moment calculation, withhold the time-critical response claim for this actuator scenario and request load/rate evidence.

fields.label: Command value for full elevator capacity (fraction)

fields.help: Movement time equals travel divided by movement speed. Use 12° and 20°/s; enter seconds. Enter a number only.

sweep.units: Normalized command dimensionless; applied and available pitching moment in N m.

experience.scenario: The trainer may have enough static capacity but still miss an actuator deadline. A synthetic actuator must move 12° at 20°/s within 0.4 s.
experience.task: Specify how the app should distinguish maximum capacity from applied moment. Calculate half-command moment and the time for a separate 12° actuator movement. You are entering display requirements and calculations, not building the interface.
experience.method: Normalized command uses 0 = none, 0.5 = half, 1 = full (not 100). Applied moment = command × capacity. Capacity remains available even at zero command. Movement time = travel / slew rate; a positive static margin does not ensure timely delivery.
experience.investigate: Inspect zero, half and full command; compare actuator movement time against the deadline. Explain the distinct static and rate statuses. In the actuator panel, compare 20, 30 and 40 degrees per second with travel and deadline fixed. Record the equality case in your explanation.
experience.tools: Only this app and its calculation pad are needed.

reflection.included: The experiment checks moment capacity and estimates movement time from travel and a constant actuator rate.
reflection.omitted: It does not include command delay, actuator acceleration or a reduction in speed under aerodynamic load.
reflection.question: What actuator measurements under load would you need before trusting the predicted time to reach the requested deflection?
reflection.help: Use one specific detail from this investigation. Explain what you would check next and why it matters; you do not need to perform that new test here.

experience.terms: An actuator moves a control surface. Its slew rate is movement speed in degrees per second. A normalized command is a fraction from 0 to 1. Here moment is assumed proportional to that fraction; this is a teaching approximation.
